title: JavaScript Project-Based Learning Applied Check
description: Test your ability to plan project milestones, choose state and data structures, debug common issues, and prepare JavaScript projects for sharing.
author: DailyCoder

questions.prompt: A student wants to build a full social network as their first JavaScript project. What is the best next step?

options.text: Define a small version one, such as posting and displaying local messages
Start with authentication, payments, and private messaging all at once
Skip requirements and write random code until it works
Avoid building any user interaction

questions.explanation: Large ideas should be reduced to a small, finishable first version with clear behavior.

questions.prompt: You are building a todo app. Which should be part of the first milestone?

options.text: Render a hard-coded list of task objects
Add cloud sync, billing, and user profiles
Deploy before any task appears on screen
Write every possible extension before testing the first feature

questions.explanation: Rendering hard-coded data is a useful early milestone because it proves the UI can display the chosen data shape.

questions.prompt: An expense tracker needs to delete individual expenses after sorting. Which data choice is most important?

options.text: Give each expense a stable `id`
Use only the array index as the permanent identifier
Store expenses only as strings with no structure
Put all expense data inside CSS class names

questions.explanation: Stable IDs allow the app to identify the correct item even when sorting changes array positions.

questions.prompt: What is the best structure for calculating an expense total?

options.text: Derive the total from the expenses array when rendering or calculating summaries
Manually update a separate total in many unrelated places
Read the total from the text currently shown in the DOM
Store the total in the CSS file

questions.explanation: Totals are derived data. Calculating them from source data avoids outdated duplicate state.

questions.prompt: A dynamic list has delete buttons added during rendering. Which event strategy can keep the code simpler?

options.text: Use event delegation on the list container and inspect the clicked button
Add duplicate listeners every time the list renders
Avoid buttons entirely because dynamic lists cannot handle events
Use `fetch()` for every click even without an API

questions.explanation: Event delegation is useful for lists whose child elements are created dynamically.

questions.prompt: An API dashboard sometimes shows an endless loading message after a failed request. What is the best fix pattern?

options.text: Clear loading state in a `finally` block and render the error state
Ignore errors because failed requests are impossible
Remove all loading UI
Use `innerHTML` to hide the problem

questions.explanation: `finally` runs after success or failure, making it a good place to clear loading state.

questions.prompt: A quiz app allows submitting a question without selecting an answer. What should happen first?

options.text: Validate the selection and show a message before changing score or moving forward
Increase the score anyway
Delete all questions
Deploy the app immediately

questions.explanation: Form and interaction validation should happen before state changes that depend on valid input.

questions.prompt: Your project crashes on startup with `Cannot read properties of null (reading 'addEventListener')`. What should you check first?

options.text: Whether the selector matches an existing element and the script runs after the element exists
Whether CSS variables are uppercase
Whether `localStorage` has enough colors
Whether all functions are arrow functions

questions.explanation: The error usually means the selected DOM element is `null`, often because the selector is wrong or the script runs too early.

questions.prompt: A search box calls an API on every keypress and feels wasteful. What improvement is often appropriate?

options.text: Debounce the search so the request waits until typing pauses
Make ten requests for every keypress
Store the API key in the DOM
Replace all JavaScript with comments

questions.explanation: Debouncing reduces repeated work for interactions like search input.

questions.prompt: A user can type a task title that is rendered on the page. Which rendering approach is safer?

options.text: Set an element's `textContent` to the title
Set `innerHTML` directly from the title
Run the title through `eval()`
Use the title as a script URL

questions.explanation: `textContent` treats the value as text instead of parsing it as HTML.

questions.prompt: Before sharing a deployed static project, what should you verify?

options.text: The deployed page loads, assets work, JavaScript runs, and core features still pass manual checks
Only that it works on your local file path
That private secrets are visible in the browser
That the README describes features that do not exist

questions.explanation: Deployment can introduce path, API, and environment issues, so the deployed version must be tested.

questions.prompt: A capstone plan includes this risk: `The current card index may point past the end after filtering.` What is the best response?

options.text: Add logic and tests for empty filtered lists and index reset behavior
Ignore it because risks never happen
Remove filtering from the README but keep the broken code
Store the index in CSS

questions.explanation: Known risks should become design decisions and test cases.

questions.prompt: Which manual test belongs in a localStorage project checklist?

options.text: Add data, refresh the page, and confirm the data is still present
Only check that the CSS file exists
Never refresh the page
Delete the README before testing

questions.explanation: Persistence features should be tested across page reloads.

questions.prompt: You finished version one and have repeated validation code in three event handlers. What is a reasonable next step?

options.text: Extract a named validation helper while preserving current behavior
Rewrite the entire project before checking that version one still works
Delete validation because duplicated code means validation is impossible
Add five unrelated features first

questions.explanation: After behavior works, extracting meaningful helpers is a useful refactoring step.

options.text: Built a quiz app with JavaScript modules, DOM rendering, score calculation, validation, and localStorage best-score persistence
Made a thing
Used JavaScript somehow
Project has many secret features but none are documented

questions.explanation: Specific descriptions communicate what the project does and which technical skills it demonstrates.
